# pbs_node_status (Data Source)

Reads how a Proxmox Backup Server node is doing: its memory, swap and root file system, its load and CPU use, its uptime, kernel and CPUs, how it booted, and the fingerprint of its certificate. The figures are those of the moment Terraform reads the data source, so most of them change from one plan to the next.

In a container, PBS sees the host's `/proc` and kernel: `memory`, `swap`, `load_average`, `cpu`, `io_wait`, `uptime`, `kernel` and `cpu_info` are the host's, unless the container uses lxcfs, while `root` is the container's own root file system.

Needs `Sys.Audit on /system/status`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "pbs_node_status" "this" {}

output "pbs_kernel" {
  value = data.pbs_node_status.this.kernel.release
}

# A warning in every plan once the root file system has less than 10 % free:
# PBS keeps its configuration, logs and task logs there.
check "pbs_root_space" {
  assert {
    condition     = data.pbs_node_status.this.root.avail > 0.1 * data.pbs_node_status.this.root.total
    error_message = "The root file system of the PBS has ${floor(data.pbs_node_status.this.root.avail / 1073741824)} GiB free."
  }
}

# A warning when memory runs short; used leaves out cache the kernel can free.
check "pbs_memory" {
  assert {
    condition     = data.pbs_node_status.this.memory.used < 0.9 * data.pbs_node_status.this.memory.total
    error_message = "The PBS uses more than 90 % of its memory."
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `node` (String) Node to read: `localhost` or the node's host name. Defaults to the provider's `node`.

### Read-Only

- `boot_mode` (String) How the node booted: `efi` or `legacy-bios`. Docker hides the firmware from its containers by default, so PBS in Docker normally reports `legacy-bios` whatever the host booted with.
- `cpu` (Number) Fraction of CPU time in use, from `0` to `1` (not a percentage), over roughly the last 1 to 10 seconds: PBS compares the kernel's CPU counters with its previous sample of them, which it takes at least every 10 seconds. Null if PBS reports no number.
- `cpu_info` (Attributes) The node's CPUs, from `/proc/cpuinfo`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cpu_info))
- `fingerprint` (String) SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate the server's web interface and API serve on port 8007 (`proxy.pem`): 32 lower-case hexadecimal pairs separated by colons. It is the same as the `fingerprint` of `pbs_fingerprint`, which needs `Sys.Modify on /system/certificates`, where this data source needs only `Sys.Audit on /system/status`.
- `io_wait` (Number) Fraction of CPU time spent idle waiting for I/O, from `0` to `1`, over the same period as `cpu`. Null if PBS reports no number.
- `kernel` (Attributes) The running kernel, as `uname` reports it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--kernel))
- `kernel_version` (String) The running kernel as one string, `<sysname> <release> <version>`, such as `Linux 6.14.11-4-pve #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC PMX 6.14.11-4 (...)`.
- `load_average` (List of Number) Load average over the last 1, 5 and 15 minutes, in that order: the average number of processes running, waiting for a CPU or waiting in uninterruptible sleep, usually for I/O.
- `memory` (Attributes) Memory of the node, from `/proc/meminfo`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--memory))
- `root` (Attributes) The root file system, `/`, as `statfs` reports it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--root))
- `secure_boot` (Boolean) Whether the node booted with UEFI Secure Boot on; always `false` with `legacy-bios`.
- `swap` (Attributes) Swap space of the node, from `/proc/meminfo`; all `0` without swap. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--swap))
- `uptime` (Number) How long the node has been up, in seconds.

<a id="nestedatt--cpu_info"></a>
### Nested Schema for `cpu_info`

Read-Only:

- `cpus` (Number) Number of logical CPUs, hyper-threads included.
- `model` (String) CPU model, such as `Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 6338 CPU @ 2.00GHz`; null when `/proc/cpuinfo` names none, as on ARM.
- `sockets` (Number) Number of CPU sockets; `0` when `/proc/cpuinfo` does not tell, as on ARM.


<a id="nestedatt--kernel"></a>
### Nested Schema for `kernel`

Read-Only:

- `machine` (String) Hardware architecture, such as `x86_64` or `aarch64`.
- `release` (String) Kernel release, such as `6.14.11-4-pve`.
- `sysname` (String) Name of the operating system, `Linux`; not the host name.
- `version` (String) Kernel build, such as `#1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC PMX 6.14.11-4 (...)`.


<a id="nestedatt--memory"></a>
### Nested Schema for `memory`

Read-Only:

- `free` (Number) Memory not used at all, not even as cache, in bytes (`MemFree`). It is usually less than `total` minus `used`.
- `total` (Number) Total memory, in bytes.
- `used` (Number) Memory in use, in bytes: `total` minus the memory the kernel reports as available (`MemAvailable`), so cache the kernel can free does not count.


<a id="nestedatt--root"></a>
### Nested Schema for `root`

Read-Only:

- `avail` (Number) Bytes free for users other than root: the blocks the file system reserves for root do not count, so it may be less than `total` minus `used`.
- `total` (Number) Size of the file system, in bytes.
- `used` (Number) Bytes in use on the file system.


<a id="nestedatt--swap"></a>
### Nested Schema for `swap`

Read-Only:

- `free` (Number) Free swap space, in bytes.
- `total` (Number) Total swap space, in bytes.
- `used` (Number) Swap space in use, in bytes: `total` minus `free`.
